decision: Keep direct filesystem-lock instrumentation and add a fail-closed p95 contention qualification evaluator before considering a database or lock daemon.

reviews.correctness: Use lock acquisition telemetry and durable mutation elapsed time from the real coordinator/journal paths. Reject missing or malformed samples and require every mutation path to pass.
reviews.robustness_security: Keep telemetry duration-only; do not expose lock owner tokens, process identities, mission payloads, or journal command contents. Require explicit finite budgets rather than implicit readiness.
reviews.latency_resources_regression: Offline percentile evaluation adds no production, Qubes, or network round trips and negligible CPU/memory. A database or daemon would add operational state and a larger regression surface before measurements justify it.

winner: direct timing evidence plus explicit p95 budget gate
why: It separates lock contention from durable commit latency using existing instrumentation, fails closed, and provides the evidence needed to decide whether same-host filesystem locking remains acceptable before Slice 2.
rejected: Infer contention from child-process wall clock: contaminated by process startup and unrelated scheduling.
Move to a database now: higher migration and operational risk without measured need.
Use a lock daemon now: adds lifecycle, IPC, and failure modes before same-host lock budgets are known.
failures_lessons: A timing metric without an explicit budget cannot gate readiness.
Lock-wait and durable-commit latency must be evaluated separately because fsync cost can dominate even when contention is low.
Synthetic unit fixtures validate the evaluator only; real p50/p95 values must come from the spawned process campaign before setting target-host budgets.
qa: Unit tests cover pass, lock-wait failure, durable-commit failure, missing samples, malformed samples, and invalid budgets. Real budgets remain intentionally unset until process-boundary measurements execute on the target host.
